paraphrase: Sleep in comfort, little nun, well wrapped in the robe you made; your passion has been stilled like herbs dried in a pot.

paraphrase: Kisāgotamī: the Sage praised good friendship; painful is the state of women, said the tamer of men — co-wives, childbirth, some who cut their throats; on the road giving birth she found her husband dead, her children dead, her family burned; she developed the eightfold path leading to the deathless, realised nibbāna, and looked into the mirror of the Dhamma.

paraphrase: Uppalavaṇṇā: seeing the danger in sensual pleasures she went forth; she knows past lives, has the divine eye, knows others' minds, and has psychic power; to Māra she replies that even a hundred thousand rogues would not shake her, she is master of her mind and has destroyed the mass of darkness.

paraphrase: Ambapālī's verses: her hair, eyes, teeth, voice, breasts and limbs, once beautiful, are now worn with age: 'such was this body; now old, it is a home of pain, a house with plaster falling; the words of the truth-speaker do not change'.

paraphrase: Verses of Cāpā: her husband Kāḷa, formerly an ascetic carrying a staff, now hunting deer, says he will cut her bonds and go forth again; she pleads with him, he leaves, and goes to the Buddha.
notes: SuttaCentral thig13.3. The verses name the man Kāḷa; the commentary identifies him with Upaka the Ājīvaka (not in the verses).

paraphrase: Ubbirī, weeping in the charnel ground for her daughter Jīvā, is told that 84,000 women named Jīvā have been burned there — which one does she mourn? The dart is drawn from her heart; grief is dispelled.

paraphrase: Somā: what does womanhood matter when the mind is well concentrated and knowledge flows, for one who rightly sees into the Dhamma; delight is everywhere destroyed, the mass of darkness is torn.

original.text: “Yaṁ taṁ isīhi pattabbaṁ, ṭhānaṁ durabhisambhavaṁ; Na taṁ dvaṅgulapaññāya, sakkā pappotumitthiyā”. “Itthibhāvo no kiṁ kayirā, cittamhi susamāhite; Ñāṇamhi vattamānamhi, sammā dhammaṁ vipassato. Sabbattha vihatā nandī, Tamokhandho padālito; Evaṁ jānāhi pāpima, Nihato tvamasi antakā”ti.

paraphrase: Paṭācārā: seeing the water she washed her feet with flow down the slope, she concentrated her mind like a thoroughbred horse; taking a lamp she entered her cell, looked at the bed, sat, and with a needle drew down the wick: at the lamp's going out her mind was liberated.

paraphrase: Bhaddā Kuṇḍalakesā, once a debater with hair plucked out, seeing faults in the faultless and none in the faulty, met the Buddha on Vulture's Peak; he said 'Come, Bhaddā' and that was her ordination; for fifty years she wandered free of debt, eating the country's alms.

paraphrase: Khemā answers Māra, who tempts her with youth and music: this rotting body disgusts me; sensual pleasures are like swords and stakes; ignorance torn apart, I once worshipped stars and fire in the forest, not knowing; now I worship the Awakened One and am freed from all suffering.

paraphrase: Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī's homage to the Buddha: all suffering is understood, craving dried up, the eightfold path developed and cessation touched; I was mother, son, father, brother, grandmother before; Māyā gave birth to Gotama for the sake of many; see the disciples in harmony — that is the homage to the Buddhas.
